texts.text:
# Trademark Policy

The AGPL-3.0 license in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) covers Arcfin's **source code**. It doesn't grant any rights to Arcfin's **name, logo, app icon or other branding**.

"Arcfin" and the Arcfin app icon and logo are trademarks of the project maintainer. They're kept separate from the code license, the same way projects such as VLC and Mozilla Firefox separate their open-source code from their trademarks.

## What you can do

Under the AGPL you're free to fork, modify, self-host and redistribute Arcfin's source code, including commercially, as long as you follow the license's terms (share the source with your users, keep the license and notices, and so on).

You can also:
- refer to Arcfin by name to describe it, review it or say your work is compatible with it;
- say your project is "a fork of Arcfin" or "based on Arcfin".

## What you can't do

- Call your fork "Arcfin", or a name confusingly similar to it.
- Use the Arcfin app icon, logo, screenshots or App Store listing assets.
- Present your fork as the official Arcfin app, or as affiliated with, endorsed by or maintained by the Arcfin project.
- Publish a build under the Arcfin name on the App Store, TestFlight or any other store.

If you fork or rebrand the project, pick your own name and icon, and say clearly in your README that it's a fork of Arcfin. That's not just allowed, it's appreciated.

## Assets excluded from the code license

App icons, marketing screenshots and other brand assets under `assets/`, and App Store Connect metadata under `fastlane/metadata/`, are **not** licensed under the AGPL. All rights to them are reserved unless a file says otherwise.

## Other projects' trademarks

Arcfin is an independent project. "Jellyfin" and the Jellyfin logo belong to the Jellyfin project, which doesn't endorse Arcfin. Arcfin uses the name only to say which server it works with, as the [Jellyfin branding guidelines](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/branding/) allow. The same goes for Seerr, TMDB, Apple, and every other product named in this repository.

## Questions

Email [support.arcfin@psmattas.com](mailto:support.arcfin@psmattas.com) if you're unsure whether a particular use is covered.

texts.title: Privacy Policy
texts.text:
Arcfin (“the app”) is developed by Puranjay Savar Mattas (“we”, “us”). This policy applies to Arcfin on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and Apple Watch, and in CarPlay.


WHAT ARCFIN CONNECTS TO

Arcfin is a client for services you run or already use. When you add a server or turn on a feature, your device talks to it directly:

• Your Jellyfin server (required). Arcfin sends your sign-in details and playback requests straight to the address you enter.

• Arcfin Sync (optional, a plugin on your Jellyfin server). If your server’s admin installs it, your synced settings are stored on that server, with a record of each device you use Arcfin on: its name, platform, app version, when it was last seen and how it syncs. The server’s admins can set defaults and locks for settings. From version 0.6 the admin can also turn on watch parties, Seerr and TMDB through the server, signed security commands, watch time limits, download limits, shared accounts, announcements, hidden titles and recommendations, and from version 0.7 notifications; each is off until they do. What these keep is listed below. All of this stays on your server; we never receive it.

• Seerr (optional). If you connect a Seerr server, your device talks to it directly for requests, your watchlist and issues you report, signed in per profile. An issue you report, with its comments, is kept by Seerr like any other.

• TMDB (optional). If you add your own TMDB API key, Arcfin asks The Movie Database for review scores, where-to-watch information, popular titles and images, using the IDs of the titles you look at.

• Wikidata. To show awards on a title page, Arcfin sends that title’s TMDB ID to Wikidata’s public query service.

• LRCLIB (optional). If you turn on Find Missing Lyrics in Settings › Music, Arcfin looks up lyrics your server doesn’t have on LRCLIB, a free lyrics library, sending it the song’s title, artist, album and length.

• YouTube (iPhone, iPad and Mac). If your server has no trailer for a title and YouTube Fallback is on in Settings › Playback, Arcfin plays its trailer from YouTube using Google’s embedded player.

• Google Cast (Chromecast, iPhone and iPad). When you cast, Google’s Cast SDK finds Cast devices on your local network, and the one you pick plays from your server.

• ListenBrainz (optional, per profile). It’s off until you add your own ListenBrainz user token in Settings › Integrations. With a token, Arcfin sends your listens to ListenBrainz, each with the song title, artist, album, its length, when you played it, and that it came from Arcfin and which Arcfin version. It also sends the loves and hates you set on a song, reads your feedback and your listening stats for Stats and Year in Music, and checks that the token is valid. If you import your listening history while ListenBrainz is linked, the plays from the files you pick are sent to ListenBrainz with their times, as well as to your Jellyfin server. The switch for this is on by default; turn it off when you import to keep those plays off ListenBrainz.

• What’s Playing? (optional, iPhone and iPad). It’s off until you turn it on in Settings › Music. To identify a song playing nearby, Arcfin uses Apple’s ShazamKit and the microphone, only while you’re on that screen. ShazamKit makes a signature of the sound on your device and matches it with Apple’s Shazam service. Arcfin doesn’t keep the recording or send it anywhere else. It then looks for the song on your server, and can open it in Apple Music.

• Apple Music (optional, iPhone and iPad). If you have an Apple Music subscription and turn on Apple Music in Settings › Music, music search also looks in Apple Music’s catalogue with MusicKit, sending Apple your search, and plays songs that aren’t on your server in Apple Music’s own player.

• Voice search in CarPlay (iPhone). Arcfin uses the microphone and Apple’s speech recognition to turn what you say into a search. Apple may process the audio under its own privacy policy. Arcfin only uses the resulting text, to search your server.

• Apple Watch. Your iPhone sends the watch your active profile’s server addresses and sign-in over Apple’s WatchConnectivity. The watch keeps the sign-in in its own Keychain and then talks to your Jellyfin server itself. Signing out on your iPhone clears it.

We operate none of these. We have no view of your library, your watch history, your requests or your settings.


WHAT’S STORED, AND WHERE

Data | Where it lives

Server addresses, sign-in tokens, Seerr sign-ins, your TMDB key and your ListenBrainz token | Your device’s Keychain, encrypted by the system. Only ever sent to the service it belongs to. If your server’s admin sets up Seerr or TMDB in the Arcfin Sync plugin, Arcfin uses them through your server instead and removes the Seerr password and TMDB key from your device.

Profile lock (PIN, Face ID, Touch ID) | Your device only. Face ID and Touch ID data never leave Apple’s Secure Enclave; Arcfin only receives a yes or no. Your PIN is never sent anywhere. If your server uses the Arcfin Sync plugin’s security features, your server’s admin can send signed commands that clear a profile’s PIN, lock or unlock it, or wipe a lost device’s downloads, and Arcfin tells the server when a profile locks after too many wrong PINs.

The sign-in on your Apple Watch | The watch’s Keychain, sent from your iPhone. Cleared when you sign out on your iPhone.

Downloaded videos, music, subtitles and artwork | Your device’s storage, for offline playback, and music you keep on your Apple Watch. Removed when you delete the download or the app.

Playback progress, caches and preferences | Your device’s app storage. Progress is also saved to your Jellyfin server, as with any Jellyfin app.

Settings and the record of your devices, if your server has the Arcfin Sync plugin | Your Jellyfin server, so your settings follow you to your other devices. You can rename or forget your devices in Settings › Server › Devices & Sync.

Arcfin Sync 0.6 features, if your server’s admin turns them on | Your Jellyfin server, for the feature to work: Security: each Arcfin device’s ID, name and which version of the server’s signing key it holds, which devices you’ve trusted, approval requests for new devices, and reports that a device saw a key that didn’t match. Watch time: your daily limits and bedtime, and how many minutes you’ve watched each day. Download limits: which titles and songs each of your devices keeps downloaded, and their sizes, to count them once across your devices. Watch parties: each party’s host, guests, title, time and the time zone each guest’s device reports, until it’s over. History: past watch parties and Pick Together sessions, with who took part and what was picked, only if the admin keeps history, and for as long as they choose. Seerr through the server: requests made while Seerr can’t be reached, until they’re sent (at most three days). The admin’s Seerr and TMDB keys are kept encrypted on the server and never sent to your device. Notifications (version 0.7): your news for two weeks (changes to your Seerr requests and issues, requests waiting for approval if you manage them, and test notifications from the admin), the last state the server saw of each Seerr request and issue, and the time and result of the last call from Seerr’s webhook. The webhook’s secret is kept encrypted. Arcfin fetches your news from your server and shows it as notifications on your device; nothing goes through Apple’s push service or us. Other features: titles you hide from Continue Watching and Next Up; on a shared account, who you said is watching, for twelve hours; announcements and maintenance the admin posts. Recommendations are worked out on the server from the watch history it already keeps, and Popular on This Server only shows titles at least two other people played.

Stats | Worked out on your device from the watch history your Jellyfin server already keeps. If you’ve linked ListenBrainz, music stats and Year in Music can come from your ListenBrainz stats instead.

Wi-Fi network name | Read on your device to switch between your server’s home and remote addresses. Only the name you mark as “home” is kept, and it’s never sent anywhere.

The app’s diagnostic log | Your device only. Share Diagnostics builds it on your device and opens the system share sheet, so you choose where it goes; nothing is sent automatically. It can include your server’s address and the titles you played, so check it before posting it publicly. Report a Problem only opens our public issue tracker in your browser.

Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, widgets, Live Activities and Handoff | Titles you watch or play can appear in Spotlight, widgets, Live Activities and Siri suggestions. Apple handles these on your device under its own privacy terms.


WHAT WE DON’T DO

• We don’t run a server your data passes through.

• The app uses no analytics, advertising, tracking or crash-reporting services of any kind.

• We don’t ask for your name, email address or an account to use the app.

• We don’t sell or share data, because we don’t collect any.


OTHER SERVICES

• Google Cast (Chromecast, iPhone and iPad only) uses Google’s Cast SDK to find and control Cast devices on your network, under Google’s Privacy Policy.

• YouTube trailers are subject to Google’s Privacy Policy and the YouTube Terms of Service.

• TMDB requests are subject to TMDB’s Privacy Policy. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

• ListenBrainz is run by the MetaBrainz Foundation, under the MetaBrainz Foundation’s Privacy Policy.

• LRCLIB (lrclib.net) is a free, open lyrics library, run independently of us under its own terms.

• Wikidata queries are subject to the Wikimedia Foundation’s Privacy Policy.

• Apple services are subject to Apple’s Privacy Policy: AirPlay, SharePlay for watching or listening together over FaceTime, Picture in Picture, Siri and Shortcuts, Spotlight, widgets, Live Activities, Handoff, notifications, CarPlay, the Apple Watch and WatchConnectivity, ShazamKit and Shazam, MusicKit and Apple Music, speech recognition, and TestFlight, including nightly builds for internal testers.

We don’t control these services and aren’t responsible for how they handle data.


PERMISSIONS

• Local Network, to find your Jellyfin server and Cast devices on your network, and for Set Up Nearby Device, which signs in an Apple TV, iPad or Mac from your iPhone or iPad on the same network. Several devices can be waiting; you set them up one at a time, and you can send several profiles in one go. For each profile you choose, your iPhone or iPad sends your Jellyfin user name, the server’s name and its addresses and, if you added them, your TMDB key, the profile’s Seerr server address, sign-in method and Seerr user name, and your ListenBrainz token. It never sends a password: Jellyfin signs in on the new device through Quick Connect, and a local Seerr account signs in on the new device itself.

• The new device sends back a Quick Connect code for each profile. Only after you’ve pressed Allow on it does it also send which Jellyfin accounts are already signed in there, so your iPhone or iPad doesn’t offer them again.

• Both screens show the same six-digit code to check first. Nothing is sent until you’ve pressed Allow on the new device, and your profiles aren’t sent until you’ve also confirmed the code on your iPhone or iPad. Everything after that is encrypted and goes directly between your devices over your local network, never to us.

• Bluetooth (iPhone and iPad), which Google Cast can use to find nearby Cast devices.

• Location, only to read the current Wi-Fi name for home and remote switching. Your location is never stored, tracked or shared.

• Face ID, only to unlock a profile you’ve locked.

• Camera (iPhone and iPad), only while you scan a code: the Quick Connect code an Apple TV shows to sign it in, or a Pick Together or watch party code. Nothing is recorded or sent.

• Microphone (iPhone and iPad), only while you’re on the What’s Playing? screen, to identify a song playing nearby, and for voice search in CarPlay.

• Speech Recognition (iPhone), to turn what you say to voice search in CarPlay into a search.

• Media & Apple Music (iPhone and iPad), only if you turn on Apple Music in Settings › Music, to find and play songs that aren’t on your server.

• Siri (iPhone and iPad), so Siri can play your movies, shows and music in Arcfin when you ask, including in the car.

• Notifications, to tell you about new episodes, downloads, your Seerr requests and issues, and your server’s announcements. Arcfin checks your own server and Seerr for them.

Each one is optional. If you say no, only the feature that needs it stops working.


THIS WEBSITE

arcfin.psmattas.com is a static site with no advertising and no tracking across other sites. Apart from Cloudflare’s own scripts described below, it loads no fonts, scripts or images from other services.

• Cloudflare delivers the site and protects it from abuse. To do that it processes your IP address and the details of each request, and it may set a security cookie such as cf_clearance or __cf_bm when it checks that a visitor isn’t an automated attack. These cookies are strictly necessary for the site to stay available and aren’t used to track you. See Cloudflare’s Privacy Policy and its cookie list.

• Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits to the site. A small script from Cloudflare reports the page you opened, the page that linked you there, your browser and device type, your country (worked out from your IP address, which isn’t stored) and how quickly the page loaded. It sets no cookies, uses no local storage and doesn’t follow you to other sites. We use these numbers to spot abuse and attacks, to see which pages people read, and to decide which languages to add next. See what Cloudflare Web Analytics collects.

• Your choices, in your browser. The site remembers your appearance (System, Light or Dark), your language and that you’ve seen the cookie notice, in your browser’s local storage under arcfin-theme, arcfin-lang and arcfin-cookies. They never leave your device, and clearing your browser’s data for the site removes them.

Because these are strictly necessary, only store a choice you made, or count visits without cookies or identifying you, the site doesn’t ask for consent. The notice at the bottom of the page is there so you know about them. To opt out of the visit counting, block static.cloudflareinsights.com with a content blocker; the site works the same without it.


CHILDREN

Arcfin isn’t directed at children. Content restrictions and parental controls are set on your Jellyfin server, and Arcfin follows them.


DELETING YOUR DATA

Deleting the app removes everything Arcfin stored on that device: downloads, caches, preferences and Keychain entries. Your library, accounts and watch history live on your Jellyfin server and aren’t affected; manage them there. Settings, device records and everything else the Arcfin Sync plugin keeps can be removed by your server’s admin from the plugin on your server. Listens and feedback you sent to ListenBrainz are managed in your ListenBrainz account.


CHANGES

If this policy changes, the new version will be posted at this address with a new effective date. The source code is public, so you can check what the app does yourself.


CONTACT

Questions about this policy: support.arcfin@psmattas.com. See also Data Protection.

texts.title: Data Protection
texts.text:
This page adds to the Privacy Policy. Both apply to Arcfin on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and Apple Watch, and in CarPlay.


DATA CONTROLLER

For the small amount of data that relates to the app itself (not your Jellyfin server’s own data), the controller is:

Puranjay Savar Mattas Contact: privacy.arcfin@psmattas.com

We haven’t appointed a Data Protection Officer, as one isn’t required for processing of this scope.


WHAT’S PROCESSED, AND ON WHAT BASIS

Data | Where it’s processed | Legal basis

Sign-ins for your Jellyfin and Seerr servers, your TMDB key and your ListenBrainz token | On your device (Keychain) and directly with the service you set up. Never with us. | Performance of a contract: providing the app’s core function (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR)

Your Seerr requests and watchlist | Your Seerr server, directly from your device | Performance of a contract; you connect Seerr

Playback progress, downloads and preferences | On your device, and on your Jellyfin server as with any Jellyfin app | Performance of a contract

Settings synced with the Arcfin Sync plugin, and a record of each device you use Arcfin on (name, platform, app version, when it was last seen and how it syncs) | Your Jellyfin server. The server’s admins can see the records and set defaults and locks. Never with us. | Performance of a contract; your server’s admin chooses to install the plugin

Arcfin Sync 0.6 features, each only if your server’s admin turns it on: device security records (device IDs, names, the signing key each holds, trusted devices, key-mismatch reports), daily minutes watched, which titles and songs each device keeps downloaded, watch parties and their guests’ time zones, optional history of watch parties and Pick Together sessions, hidden titles, queued Seerr requests, who’s watching on a shared account, and from version 0.7 your notifications and the last state of each Seerr request and issue | Your Jellyfin server, kept by the plugin. History is kept only if, and for as long as, the admin chooses; queued Seerr requests for at most three days; who’s watching for twelve hours; notifications for two weeks. Never with us. | Legitimate interests of the server’s admin in running their server safely and for their household; your server’s admin chooses to turn each feature on

IDs of titles you open, sent to TMDB and Wikidata | Those services, directly from your device | Legitimate interest in showing title information; TMDB only if you add a key

A song’s title, artist, album and length, to look up lyrics your server doesn’t have | LRCLIB, directly from your device, only if you turn on Find Missing Lyrics | Consent: you turn the setting on, and can turn it off at any time

The trailer you play when your server has none (iPhone, iPad and Mac) | YouTube, through Google’s embedded player, while YouTube Fallback is on in Settings › Playback | Performance of a contract; you can turn the setting off

What you cast (Chromecast, iPhone and iPad) | Google’s Cast SDK finds Cast devices on your local network, and the one you pick plays from your server | Performance of a contract; you start casting. Bluetooth, if you allow it, through the system prompt.

With ListenBrainz linked: your listens (the song title, artist, album, its length, when you played it, and that it came from Arcfin and which Arcfin version), the loves and hates you set on songs, and, if you import your listening history, the plays from the files you pick with their times (the import’s switch for this is on by default and can be turned off) | ListenBrainz, run by the MetaBrainz Foundation, directly from your device. Arcfin also reads your feedback and stats from it and checks the token. The token is kept in your device’s Keychain for that profile. Never with us. | Consent: you add your own token, and you can remove it at any time

Sound from the microphone while you’re on the What’s Playing? screen (iPhone and iPad) | ShazamKit makes a signature of the sound on your device and Apple’s Shazam service matches it, under Apple’s privacy policy. Arcfin doesn’t keep the recording or send it anywhere else. | Consent: What’s Playing? is off until you turn it on, and the system asks for the microphone

Your music searches, with the Apple Music option on (iPhone and iPad) | Apple Music’s catalogue, searched with MusicKit; songs that aren’t on your server play in Apple Music’s own player, under Apple’s privacy policy | Consent: the option is off until you turn it on, and the system asks for Media & Apple Music

What you say to voice search in CarPlay | Apple’s speech recognition, which may process the audio under Apple’s privacy policy. Arcfin only uses the resulting text, to search your server. | Consent, through the system’s Microphone and Speech Recognition prompts

Your active profile’s server addresses and sign-in, sent to your Apple Watch | Sent from your iPhone over Apple’s WatchConnectivity and kept in the watch’s Keychain; the watch then talks to your Jellyfin server itself. Cleared when you sign out on your iPhone. | Performance of a contract

Titles shown in Siri suggestions, Shortcuts, Spotlight, widgets, Live Activities and Handoff | On your devices, handled by Apple under its own privacy terms | Performance of a contract; Siri through the system’s Siri prompt

What you play with AirPlay or SharePlay, or in CarPlay | The devices and Apple services you choose, under Apple’s privacy policy. SharePlay shares what you watch or listen to with the people on your FaceTime call. | Performance of a contract; you start it

Set Up Nearby Device, which signs in an Apple TV, iPad or Mac from your iPhone or iPad. For each profile you choose, your iPhone or iPad sends your Jellyfin user name, the server’s name and its addresses and, if you added them, your TMDB key, the profile’s Seerr server address, sign-in method and Seerr user name, and your ListenBrainz token. It never sends a password: Jellyfin signs in on the new device through Quick Connect, and a local Seerr account signs in on the new device itself. The new device sends back a Quick Connect code for each profile. Only after you’ve pressed Allow on it does it also send which Jellyfin accounts are already signed in there, so your iPhone or iPad doesn’t offer them again. | Sent directly between your devices over your local network, encrypted. Nothing is sent until you’ve pressed Allow on the new device, and your profiles aren’t sent until you’ve also confirmed the same code on your iPhone or iPad. Never with us. | Performance of a contract; you start it and confirm it on both devices

The Quick Connect code and server address in an Apple TV’s QR code | On your devices. If the link opens this website, the page reads them in your browser; browsers don’t send that part of a link, so they never reach the site. | Performance of a contract

The camera image while you scan an Apple TV’s code | On your device only; nothing is recorded or sent | Consent, through the system’s camera prompt. Decline it and you can still type the code.

Wi-Fi network name | On your device only | Consent, through the system’s location prompt. Decline it and home switching simply won’t happen.

Diagnostic log | On your device. Share Diagnostics opens the system share sheet, so it goes only where you send it; nothing is sent automatically. | Consent: you choose whether and where to send it

Crash reports and TestFlight feedback you share with Apple | Apple, under its own policies. We only see them if Apple shares them with developers under your device’s settings and TestFlight. | Your choice in your device’s settings and in TestFlight

Visits to this website (IP address, request details, Cloudflare security cookies) | Cloudflare, which delivers and protects arcfin.psmattas.com | Legitimate interest in keeping the site available and secure (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR)

Visit statistics for this website (page, referring page, browser and device type, country, load time) | Cloudflare Web Analytics; no cookies, and your IP address isn’t stored | Legitimate interest in keeping the site secure and improving it, for example choosing which languages to add (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR)

Your appearance and language choices on this website | Your browser’s local storage only | Storing a choice you made; strictly necessary

We don’t process any data for advertising, profiling or automated decision-making.


YOUR JELLYFIN SERVER’S DATA

Your watch history, library, user accounts and similar data live on your Jellyfin server (and Seerr, if connected), which you or someone you trust controls. We aren’t the controller or processor of that data. Requests to access, correct or delete it go to whoever runs that server, which may be you.


RECIPIENTS

We receive none of the app’s data. Depending on what you set up or turn on, your device sends data directly to your Jellyfin server and the Arcfin Sync plugin on it, Seerr, TMDB, Wikidata, LRCLIB, ListenBrainz, YouTube, Google Cast devices and Apple. None of them processes data on our behalf; each handles it under its own terms and privacy policy, listed in the Privacy Policy.


INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS

Because Arcfin has no server, none of your data is transferred to us. Data goes directly from your device to the services you set up, wherever they’re hosted.


RETENTION

Data on your device is kept until you delete it, sign out or delete the app. We hold nothing on a server, so there’s nothing for us to retain. What you send to your Jellyfin server, Seerr or ListenBrainz is kept under their own policies.


YOUR RIGHTS

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict or port data about you, to object to processing, and to withdraw consent at any time. In practice:

• Access, deletion and portability: the data is on your device, and deleting the app deletes it.

• Withdrawing consent: turn off Local Network, Location, Camera, Microphone, Speech Recognition, Media & Apple Music, Siri or other permissions in your device’s settings at any time, remove your ListenBrainz token in Settings › Integrations, or turn off Find Missing Lyrics, What’s Playing? or Apple Music in Settings › Music. The features that need them will stop working.

• Anything else: email privacy.arcfin@psmattas.com and we’ll reply within 30 days.

In the UK and EU you can also complain to your data protection authority; in the UK that’s the Information Commissioner’s Office.


CALIFORNIA RESIDENTS (CCPA/CPRA)

We don’t sell or share personal information, and haven’t in the past 12 months, because we don’t collect any. Since we hold no personal information on a server, there’s nothing further to disclose in response to an access request.


SECURITY

Sign-ins are stored in the system Keychain, encrypted by the operating system. Requests to your server use the transport your server is set up for. We strongly recommend HTTPS for any server reachable from outside your home.

Set Up Nearby Device, which signs in an Apple TV, iPad or Mac from an iPhone or iPad, agrees fresh keys on each try and shows a six-digit code from them on both screens, so a device in between can’t take part unnoticed. The new device takes one try at a time, with a pause between tries. Nothing is sent until you’ve pressed Allow on the new device, and your profiles aren’t sent until you’ve also confirmed the code on your iPhone or iPad. Everything after that is encrypted and goes directly between your devices over your local network, never to us.


CHANGES

If this page changes, the new version will be posted at this address with a new effective date.


CONTACT
